scope: Read-only targeted retained public fixture and pinned native tool-observer source; no new trial or original input.

mockSdkUsage.kind: synthetic fixture values, not actual model billing

independentRolloutMetadata.boundBy: Exact thread_id from this public outgoing native capture; no other thread contents inspected.

establishedTransition: The native rollout proves sixteen completed built-in command executions and matching function outputs. The evaluator recorded zero pre-dispatch/settled tool rows and set coverage false on an uncorrelated item/completed. This is a benchmark-observer coverage failure; zero observed tool rows is not zero native execution.
notEstablished: The adapter did not retain the exact live notification that first set coverage false; its precise item type/id and first-stop ordering remain UNKNOWN. The rollout uses PascalCase item variants, whereas the app-server source uses camelCase; no casing-fix conclusion follows from that difference alone.
The retained record does not establish why the pre-tool observer was absent: event planning, invocation, early policy refusal or another path cannot be distinguished solely from zero rows.
No complete three-turn/two-session loop, original tool-cap enforcement/refusal or full native/background close was established.

sourceBoundaries.finding: The adapter reserves through nativeToolBefore/dynamicTool, settles through nativeToolAfter/dynamicTool, and stops on an uncorrelated completion. Its existing load hook patches function bodies but does not itself declare required native relay events.

exec_command normalizes to exec. PreToolUse is conditional on executionAdmission, existing policy or configured loop detection; PostToolUse is separately conditional on an after hook/result middleware. runNativeHookRelayPreToolUse performs ordinary policy first, then executionAdmission.admit. A loaded module does not prove the callbacks are enabled or reached.

The ordinary plugin creates an owned relay and uses executionAdmission{toolNames:[exec],admit} when nativeProcessAuthority exists. buildCodexNativeHookRelayConfig emits synchronous trusted native hooks only for selected events whose shouldRelayEvent is true.

The existing ordinary binding supplies process admission only with nativeProcessAuthority and nativeToolSurfaceEnabled; nativeProcessAuthority construction is conditional on sandbox backend plus retainSourceAuthority. No claim that omitted public sandbox config alone proves the actual evaluated runtime branch.

Native closeAndWait deliberately reports cleanup uncertain after nativeExecutionObserved. Native command notifications set that flag. Thus a command-capable sample cannot infer complete native shutdown only from a closed app-server process or force this flag to closed.

smallestExistingBinding.api: registerOwnedNativeHookRelay (native-hook-relay export i), reached by existing registerNativeHookRelayForBundledRuntime/createCodexNativeHookRelay; executionAdmission{toolNames,admit(invocation,assertAdmissionCurrent)}
smallestExistingBinding.necessaryWork: Connect evaluator cap accounting to the actual owned pre-execution admission while preserving existing native policy, authority, canonical tool aliases and exact thread/turn/tool IDs. Retain/correlate native completion as a post-execution observation. Do not fabricate reservations from item/started or completion, bypass native policy, or treat module loading as admission coverage.
smallestExistingBinding.scopeLimit: The existing private API is a concrete source seam, not a newly validated all-tools binding. Coverage of other built-ins, dynamic tools/helpers and the native post/close path still needs bounded source and execution evidence before an original sample.
smallestExistingBinding.closure: Reuse independent thread/read(includeTurns), thread/backgroundTerminals/list, actual native process authority/physical transport exit and parent acknowledgement. Preserve cleanup uncertain unless those original settlement conditions are independently demonstrated.

interpretation: Calendar and mock transport progress are retained. The failure is not a product-quality loss and does not change original criteria, tool cap, source versions or closed outcomes. No immediate original admission or replay is authorized.
